# @metator/cli

<!-- metator:generated:start -->

## Responsibility

Driving adapter on commander: one module per command group, JSON-only output, exit codes. `guard *` commands answer hooks in the host's protocol instead of the envelope (ADR-0038). Each command says what it is where it is registered (`meta(cmd, {...})`, `src/command-meta.ts`): its audience, whether it only reads, the folder and check lists, and the text a person reads (`src/render.ts`), which goes to stderr at a terminal while stdout keeps the JSON line. A renamed command keeps its old words as a hidden spelling (`renamedCommand`). There is no full-screen terminal view (ADR-0086 withdrew `metator ui`); the prompts that remain are `@clack/prompts` in `src/terminal.ts`.

## Invariants

- Commander never prints; every outcome becomes one JSON envelope [[cite: packages/cli/src/program.ts:104 | ".configureOutput({ writeOut: () => {}, writeErr: () => {} })"]].

## Allowed dependencies

`@metator/core` and `@metator/runtime`. Commands resolve use cases from the container and never construct adapters (MT-ARCH-007).

## Pitfalls

- Validate option values with commander (`choices`, `argParser`), not by hand (MT-CODE-004).
- One flag name per meaning: a list of files is `--files`, a time limit is `--timeout` (`FLAG_NAMES` in `src/options.ts`, pinned by `test/flag-names.test.ts`). A renamed flag keeps its old spelling as `renamedOption`, hidden from the help and the reference.
- An MCP tool only reads (`src/mcp.ts`): a command is a tool only when it says `reads` in its `meta(...)`; an option of it that writes or runs the project's scripts goes into `writesWith` (refused), or `readsWith` names the option the tool always passes to stay read-only (`plan scope --dry-run`). A tool keeps its name when its command is renamed.
- A renamed command keeps its old words through `renamedCommand` (hidden from the help and the reference); `test/command-meta.test.ts` lists every old spelling and pins that the lists derived from `meta(...)` are the ones that were kept by hand.
- Text for a person goes to stderr only at a terminal and only from a command's `render`; stdout must stay byte-identical with and without a terminal (`test/command-meta.test.ts`).
- Who acts is one rule (`who()` in `src/who.ts`): `--by`, `$METATOR_USER`, git's `user.name`, the login name. Never record a made-up name; an approval keeps `--by` required (`byOption(..., "required")`).
- Warnings go out once, in the envelope: a command strips them from its data unless the data is a stored document whose schema has the field (`discover`).
- A new command must be added to the help list in `e2e/cli.e2e.test.ts`.
- What a person does to a run lives in core, once (`StartRun`, `AnswerQuestion`, `BriefRun`, `ReviveRuns`, `EndRun`, `EnsureDriven`, `StartDrive`): a command and a daemon route only read their input and shape their output. The CLI gives three adapters through `bootstrap` (`src/sessions.ts`): `detachedDrive` (this program's own command line for `run drive`), `runPanes` (the daemon over HTTP, or the daemon's own panes inside it) and `conductorSessions` (a run's conductor session opened by the daemon of its repository, `POST /runs/:run/start`, also from inside the daemon; no daemon is an error and core drives the run instead, ADR-0090). Never start a drive, open a conductor or close panes any other way.
- The daemon (`src/serve/`): routes are data (`routes/*.ts`: `{method, pattern, body, handler}`), and `http.ts` dispatches them: the repository's container, the body checked by its zod schema (what does not fit is 400 USAGE), the envelope through `toEnvelope`, 404 for NOT_FOUND, 403 from a `guard`. Add a route to the table (pinned by `test/serve-http.test.ts`), never an `if` in `server.ts`. Sockets are `sockets.ts`, the clocks `timers.ts`. The state and inbox sockets read one overview per repository per tick (`overviewOf` in `server.ts`); a request that is not a GET clears it. Do not build a container per poll.
- A socket on `/ws/pty/<run>` only finds the run's session; starting one is `POST /runs/<run>/pty-open`.
- `metator serve` pauses every live session when it stops and resumes them when it starts (`--no-restore`: they stay paused; `--screens-ms`: how often screens are kept on disk); `POST /runs/:run/continue` builds `ContinueTask` over every served repository's `taskRepository`, and `metator run continue` goes through it when a daemon serves the repository (ADR-0092).
- `/inbox` has `decisions`, `escalated` and `panes`: the questions of panes without a run (`PaneQuestions`, ADR-0091), each with its pane's label and role. `POST /panes/:pane/answer` answers one and is a person's only (`personOnly`).
- `quick`, `scratch` and `session` are thin: `quick fit` and `quick ready` are gate commands (exit 4 while the person has not answered; `--wait` looks again for up to 9 minutes), `scratch` works on the checkout the command runs in, and `session` goes through the daemon (`/sessions`, `/panes/:pane/tell|interrupt`), which knows the caller by its pane token: the task's main chat or, without a token, a person.
- `guard user-prompt` also tells the daemon what the person sent in a run's pane (`/panes/:pane/said`, the pane's own token); the daemon decides whether the task's main chat hears of it.
- `/runs/:run/start` is open to a person, the run's conductor and the chat a person talks in (`starterOnly`, `mayStartConductor`); every other steering route stays `conductorOnly`.
- A hook must not fail the host's tool call: `guard *` always exits 0 and reports its own errors as `systemMessage`.
- `thread` goes through the daemon when one serves the repository, else works on the files (`thread new` then makes the thread without its chat, `noPane`; `thread reopen` needs the daemon); `--thread` defaults to the thread whose chat pane runs the command (`$METATOR_PANE_ID`). `/threads` routes are `global`: in a folder they read every repository's threads and runs together (`daemon.overviews`, the state socket's cached overviews) and find the repository that holds a thread. `POST /panes/:pane/started-run` links the run to the pane's thread; the sweep adds the facts of finished runs after the chat notices. The state carries `threads` (`Threads.mark`), which is how a client learns that a thread changed.
- The Backlog's buttons (ADR-0096) are routes over `BacklogWork`: `POST /issues/:issue/analyze` opens the guide's pane, `plan` and `start` always open the run's conductor (`session`), and `start` opens the new thread's chat (`chat: true`); the CLI's `issue plan|start` open the conductor only with `--session`, and `issue start` makes a thread without its chat. `issue analyze` takes the thread from `$METATOR_PANE_ID`. `GET /issues` lists `IssueView`s (freshness, children, waitsFor, progress); `issue list|show` print the same.
- Reviews (ADR-0097) are routes over `WatchedReviews` and `MyReviews` (`routes/reviews.ts`): `POST /reviews` is global and reviews in the repository whose checkout is the MR's; `/reviews/:id/approve` is a person's only (a pane's token is refused); `/inbox` carries `reviews` (the cards of every served repository, `reviewCards`). The daemon's clock reads the watched MRs (`watchedReviews.check`) on `codehost.review.everyMs`, switched with `--reviews-ms` like the reviews of my requests. `review open|rereview` open the run's conductor unless `--no-session`; `mrs analyse` goes through the daemon.
- Only the command a person typed may ask questions (`ctx.prompter`, set by `main.ts` for a TTY); questions go to stderr so stdout stays one envelope, and commands run through `invoke` never ask (ADR-0049).
